entries.label: Avenue
entries.reason: Authored street class. Street types are discussed in NACTO Urban Street Design Guide (Island Press, 2013), Streets, which was not re-read in this build and is not quoted; these classes and ranges are this grammar's own. An avenue's kerb lanes carry traffic, so this grammar gives it no kerbside parking lane. Kerbside parking is authored, not quoted from a standard.

entries.label: High street
entries.reason: Authored street class. Street types are discussed in NACTO Urban Street Design Guide (Island Press, 2013), Streets, which was not re-read in this build and is not quoted; these classes and ranges are this grammar's own. A high street keeps a kerbside parking lane on each side, where shoppers' and deliveries' vehicles stand. Kerbside parking is authored, not quoted from a standard.

entries.label: Local street
entries.reason: Authored street class. Street types are discussed in NACTO Urban Street Design Guide (Island Press, 2013), Streets, which was not re-read in this build and is not quoted; these classes and ranges are this grammar's own. A local street keeps no kerbside parking lane in this edition, so its cross-section, and the blocks and lots it bounds, are edition 2's. Kerbside parking is authored, not quoted from a standard.

entries.label: Narrow street
entries.reason: Authored street class. Street types are discussed in NACTO Urban Street Design Guide (Island Press, 2013), Streets, which was not re-read in this build and is not quoted; these classes and ranges are this grammar's own. A narrow street has no room beside its lanes for a parked vehicle, so it has no kerbside parking lane. Kerbside parking is authored, not quoted from a standard.
